evidence_adequacy.verdict: THIN: 5 transitions constrain rank 3 of 679 features, so the null space has dimension 676 and nearly every vector in it is a 'law' that is true over these states and unfalsified rather than confirmed. Treat every law below as a correlation awaiting a transition that could break it, not as a conservation law.

log.subject: previous manual's entire word_table (Glyph9, Vacated, Spent, Dark, spawn_probe)
log.why: the store now reports 6 states, dynamic box rows 29-54 cols 10-63, 97 dynamic cells, 3999 constant and colour 14 present; the previous census claimed 34 states, 87 dynamic, 4009 constant and no colour 14, so not one number transfers and the declarations describe a different level.

log.subject: landmark spawn_probe with '# arc-cell: carried, coordinates stripped'
log.why: the grammar states a landmark without a '# arc-cell: (row, col)' comment is a hard compile error; this is the most likely single cause of 'generated/theory.py could not be loaded', and the new manual declares no landmark at all so the error cannot recur.

log.subject: mdl_segmenter obj0/obj2/obj3 (13x36, 436-440 cells)
log.why: both segmenter variants report negative gain (-4037 and -10409 bits), so by constraint 3 the segmentation costs more than the pixels it explains, and the tracks are floor-swallowing blobs 440 cells wide against a dynamic set of 97.

log.subject: mdl_segmenter obj1 (2x54, 108 cells, all 6 frames)
log.why: it spans two rows of which only one cell, (53,63), has ever changed; taking it as an object would claim 107 constant cells the board already explains.

log.as: Ink1 9, Ink2 10, Ink3 8, Dark 12, Frame6 22, Field 12, Ground 24
log.subject: the 97 dynamic cells, typed by frame-0 colour
log.why: the diffs force the dynamic set to be 96 cells in rows 30-41 cols 11-22 plus (53,63) = 97; the current frame shows exactly 24 colour-5 cells in that box, and 97-24 = 73 reproduces cells_needing_an_owner exactly, which is a number I did not compute.

log.subject: 12 dynamic cells of frame-0 colour 4 in rows 30-41 cols 17-22
log.why: forced by the census residue (73 owned minus 61 I can locate), and the arm seats them by colour without needing me to know their addresses; their location is recorded as an open guess in the manual, not as a claim.

log.subject: cegis_miner verdict 'the world does not narrate as one mover'
log.why: checked against the three itemised transitions: every one of the 25 changes is a recolour in place and no cell's position changes, so the manual contains no moved() event anywhere and the miner's refusals are correct rather than a fixture limitation.

log.subject: key3_strip_blanks_ink1 / key3_strip_blanks_ink2
log.why: t3 itemises all 12 cells of rows 38-39 cols 17-22 going to colour 4; the guard colored(above(above(?p)), 4) was checked against all 19 Ink1 and Ink2 instances and passes exactly the 12 targets.

log.subject: key7_strip_blanks_ink1 / key7_strip_blanks_ink2
log.why: t5 itemises the identical 12 cells with the identical result; ACTION3 and ACTION7 are separate rules because they are separate keys, and their only observed difference (2 frames against 1) is discarded by cascade single_frame.

log.subject: key4_strip_restores_ink1 / key4_strip_restores_ink2
log.why: t4 restores the 2,1,1,2,1,1 / 1,1,2,1,1,2 diagonal; because instances are typed by frame-0 colour, 'recolour every Ink1 reading 4 back to 1' reproduces the pattern with no coordinates, and no non-strip Ink1 or Ink2 instance reads 4 in that state.

log.subject: key4_meter_burns_right_end
log.why: one witness, t4, (53,63) 2->3; rightof(?p) = wall is unique to that instance among all ten Ink2 cells; accepted as the shortest expressible shadow of a law I have only one datum for, and the two rival readings are recorded live rather than suppressed.

log.subject: any rule for ACTION1 or ACTION2
log.why: the diff reports only 'rows 30-41, cols 11-22' and a preserved colour multiset; a 96-cell change with that description is equally a shift, a rotation, a swap or a repaint, and a wrong 96-cell rule would cascade into the strip rules and be harder to detect than an admitted hole.

log.subject: colored(below(?p), 4) as the strip guard
log.why: it is shorter but it also matches (53,63), because row 54 is solid colour 4 from edge to edge; caught by checking all ten Ink2 instances instead of the four obvious ones.

log.subject: s0 = s2, i.e. ACTION2 exactly undoes ACTION1
log.why: distinct_states 5 against 6 states forces exactly one coinciding pair; s2..s5 are pairwise distinct by their itemised diffs, so the only pair available is s0 and s2.

log.subject: zero_space global law (list of 97 cells) and its THIN self-report
log.why: its support set is my dynamic set and it says so itself: 5 transitions constrain rank 3 of 679 features, null space dimension 676, so it corroborates the census and asserts nothing beyond it.

log.subject: burn keyed to command-index parity (carried over from the previous world)
log.why: t2 is an even-index command and (53,63) did not change at t2; the reading is dead here in one line, and no belief from the previous world was carried in unchecked.

log.subject: invariant counts 9/10/8/12/22/12/24 and board 3999
log.why: they sum to 97 = dynamic_cells, their non-background part sums to 73 = cells_needing_an_owner, and 4096-97 = 3999 = constant_cells; three store numbers hit independently, marked [status: counted] rather than proven.

log.subject: press ACTION1
log.why: the only way to see the 96 cells the diff channel refuses to itemise is to receive the next full frame and subtract this one; ACTION2 provably restores the state, so the probe is free, and it closes the manual's largest defect.

log.subject: press ACTION5 or ACTION6
log.why: two of seven keys have never been pressed, my manual predicts silence for both with no witness of any kind, and either outcome is new information.

log.subject: ACTION4 pressed, then ACTION4 again after a restore
log.why: separates the key-keyed burn from the restore-event-keyed burn from a hidden counter, but it needs two commands and is ranked below the one-command probes.

log.subject: ACTION7 returning one frame while ACTION3 returns two
log.why: the only evidence the two keys differ at all; free to check on any command, and cascade single_frame means my manual cannot use it either way.

log.subject: no rule can draw the first change of (53,62)
log.why: I wanted an instance on the next cell of the row-53 bar; the arm seats instances only on cells the board cannot explain, so a never-varying cell gets none. I wrote a theorem pricing the loss at exactly one pixel per burn instead, and rejected both the second-type-on-colour-2 and the landmark workarounds as constraint-5 double claims.

log.subject: no rule can express a click's coordinates
log.why: if ACTION5 or ACTION6 is a click, act=key(5) has nowhere to put a row and a column, so the rule would fire on every click anywhere. I wrote the limitation into two_keys_have_never_been_pressed_and_one_of_them_may_be_a_click rather than invent syntax.

log.subject: the manual cannot say 'unobserved, I decline to predict'
log.why: the compiled step is total, so the absence of an ACTION1 rule reads as 'nothing happens' in the same voice as a witnessed silence. I wrote the_ninety_six_cell_hole_and_how_it_closes to make the forged silence visible in prose, and the playbook ranks the command that removes it first.
